source_name_as_recorded: Jiahan Du, “Restricted Marstrand's projection theorem for general families of linear subspaces”, arXiv:2510.16671 (2025).
statement:
Let $P_t:\mathbb{R}^n\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^m$ be an analytic family of linear maps. Define $f:[0,n]\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ as follows: for an integer $x\in[0,n]$, let $f(x)$ be the largest integer such that every subspace $A\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\dim A=x$ satisfies

$$
\dim P_t(A)\geq f(x)
$$

for all but finitely many $t\in[0,1]$; for noninteger $x$, define $f$ linearly on $[\lfloor x\rfloor,\lfloor x\rfloor+1]$. **Generalized restricted Marstrand conjecture.** For every Borel set $A\subset\mathbb{R}^n$,

$$
\dim_H P_t(A)\geq f(\dim_H A)
$$

for almost every $t\in[0,1]$. This is a more general lower-bound formulation of the restricted Marstrand problem, allowing the expected projection dimension to be determined by the eventual behavior of the family on subspaces.
technical_disposition: All analytic linear families and every Borel set require a dimension lower bound at almost every parameter. Subspace rank control does not supply an energy estimate for arbitrary fractals; integer-rank examples do not resolve interpolation. No full-scope route.
title: Generalized restricted Marstrand conjecture for analytic linear families

source_name_as_recorded: Quanyu Tang and Shu Zhang, “Generalizing Lee's conjecture on the sum of absolute values of matrices”, arXiv:2510.16846 (2025).
statement:
Let $M_n(\mathbb C)=\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, and for $A\in M_n(\mathbb C)$ write $|A|=(A^*A)^{1/2}$. For $p>1$ and $m\geq2$, let $c_p(m)$ be the smallest number such that

$$
\left\|\sum_{k=1}^m A_k\right\|_p\leq c_p(m)\left\|\sum_{k=1}^m|A_k|\right\|_p
$$

for all $A_1,\dots,A_m\in M_n(\mathbb C)$. **The closed-form conjecture.** If $x_{p,m}>0$ is the positive solution of

$$
x^p-2x-(m-1)=0,
$$

then

$$
c_p(m)=\frac{\sqrt{x_{p,m}(x_{p,m}+m-1)}}{\left(x_{p,m}^{\,p}+m-1\right)^{1/p}}.
$$

This conjecture extends Lee's problem from two matrices to an arbitrary number of matrices and is motivated by numerical experiments. The paper notes that the formula recovers the known cases $p=1,2,\infty$, while the optimal value for general $p>1$ is the unresolved issue addressed by the conjecture.
technical_disposition: Uniform over arbitrary complex matrices, all p>1 and m>=2. Scalar/rank-one lower witnesses do not prove the noncommutative upper bound; p=2 is only an instance. No uniform sharp mechanism survives statement screening.
title: The closed-form conjecture for the optimal Schatten norm constant for m matrices

source_name_as_recorded: Paul Hamrick and Gary Hu, “Lower Bounds on Intersection Families for Certain Graphs”, arXiv:2510.18064 (2025).
statement:
Let $P_4$ denote the path on four vertices, and let a $P_4$-intersecting family be a family of subgraphs of $K_n$ such that the edge intersection of any two members contains a copy of $P_4$. An **extremal family** is one having maximum possible size.

**Christofides bound conjecture.** For $n \ge 6$, the maximum size of a $P_4$-intersecting family is

$$
\frac{17}{128} \cdot 2^{\binom n2}.
$$

Furthermore, any extremal family is isomorphic to one generated by the Christofides construction.

The conjecture asks whether the Christofides construction gives the optimal density and classifies all extremal families. The source states that its optimality remains open and notes its connection with the Alon–Spencer conjecture.
technical_disposition: For every n>=6 both optimal density and uniqueness of extremizers are required. An n=6 family enumeration would not establish all-n classification; no compression/stability mechanism supplied. No enumeration executed.
title: The Christofides bound conjecture for P₄-intersecting families

source_name_as_recorded: Paul Bastide, Anurag Bishnoi, Carla Groenland, Dion Gijswijt and Rohinee Joshi, “Circular sorting, strong complete mappings and wreath product constructions”, arXiv:2510.18529 (2026).
statement:
Let $t(n)$ be the maximum number of transpositions needed to sort a circular permutation of size $n$, and define the **circular sorting defect** by

$$
c(n)=n-t(n).
$$

**Multiplicative monotonicity conjecture.** Is

$$
c(nm)\geq c(n)
$$

for all integers $n,m\geq 2$?

This asks whether multiplying the size can never decrease the defect relative to the original size. The paper presents it as a different possible notion of monotonicity, and its status remains open.
technical_disposition: All n,m>=2 compare worst-case circular transposition defects. A product construction would need a uniform bound on every circular permutation at size nm, not just a convenient product permutation. No such bridge; finite values insufficient.
title: Multiplicative monotonicity of the circular sorting defect

source_name_as_recorded: Luke Postle, “Refined Absorption: A New Proof of the Existence Conjecture and its Applications to Extremal and Probabilistic Design Theory”, arXiv:2510.19978 (2025).
statement: A **$(j,i)$-configuration** in a family of sets is a collection of $i$ members spanning at most $j$ ground-set elements; the girth of a triangle packing is the smallest $i\geq 2$ for which it contains an $(i+2,i)$-configuration. **Erdős' conjecture.** For every integer $g\geq 3$, every sufficiently large $K_3$-divisible complete graph admits a $K_3$-decomposition with girth at least $g$. The source states that Kwan, Sah, Sawhney, and Simkin proved this conjecture in full, so it is solved.
technical_disposition: Literal statement explicitly reports full Kwan-Sah-Sawhney-Simkin resolution for each fixed girth and sufficiently large admissible order. No novelty inference from open metadata; primary proof body not read here. Do not invest in rediscovery.
title: Erdős' high-girth Steiner triple system conjecture

source_name_as_recorded: Calin Chindris, Min Hyeok Kang and Daniel Kline, “The Jordan type of a multiparameter persistence module”, arXiv:2510.22116 (2025).
statement:
Let $\mathscr{P}$ be a finite poset, and let $B_1$ and $B_2$ be $\mathscr{P}$-persistence sets. Write $L_{B_1}$ and $L_{B_2}$ for their linearizations, and let $\mathrm{multirank}_{L_B}(S_1,S_2)$ denote the multirank associated with a pair of slices $(S_1,S_2)$. **Thomas's multirank conjecture.** If

$$
\mathrm{multirank}_{L_{B_1}}(S_1,S_2)=\mathrm{multirank}_{L_{B_2}}(S_1,S_2)
$$

for all pairs of slices $(S_1,S_2)$, then

$$
L_{B_1}\cong L_{B_2}.
$$

The statement asserts that multirank invariants completely determine the linearizations of finite-poset persistence sets. In the paper it is presented as Thomas's conjecture and is proved for the setting under consideration, so the claim is solved.
technical_disposition: Literal statement explicitly says this all-slice multirank classification is proved in the cited paper. Isomorphism of linearizations is not isomorphism of persistence sets. Primary proof body unread; no proposed discovery.
title: Thomas's multirank conjecture for linearizations

source_name_as_recorded: Anjali Bhagat, Tanmay Kulkarni, Urban Larsson and Divya Murali, “Tie-breaking in self interest cumulative subtraction games”, arXiv:2510.24280 (2026).
statement:
Let $S=\{s_3,s_2,s_1\}$ with $s_3<s_2<s_1$, and suppose the largest subtraction is additive:

$$
s_1=s_3+s_2.
$$

Let a friendly/antagonistic discrepancy mean a difference between the FvF and AvA self-interest games. **Additive discrepancy conjecture.** There exists a heap with a friendly/antagonistic discrepancy if and only if

$$
\frac{s_2}{s_3}\neq k
$$

for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$. When this holds, the first such heap is

$$
x=(i+2)s_2+is_1=is_3+(2i+2)s_2,
$$

where $i\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfies

$$
i+1>\frac{s_2}{s_3}>i.
$$

The statement is based on the paper's computational investigation and is presented without a proof.
technical_disposition: Primary v1 Conjecture14 and v2 matching passage read. Exact own-score-maximizing recurrence with opponent-score min/max tie-break read. Full iff includes absence at every heap in integer-ratio case and first-discrepancy minimality otherwise. Two-action monotonicity theorem does not settle three-action recurrence; no all-heap period/invariant route. Follow-up [28] body unread; no game sweep invested.
title: The additive three-action friendly-versus-antagonistic discrepancy criterion

source_name_as_recorded: Ze Xu, “Motivic multiplicativity of complete intersections”, arXiv:2511.01362 (2026).
statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth connected projective variety of dimension $n$ equipped with a CK decomposition. For an integer $m\geq 2$, an $m$-fold $r$-multiplicative CK decomposition is one whose $(m+1)$-fold intersection product respects the CK grading up to defect $r$; denote the smallest such defect by $\mathfrak{d}_m(X)$. **The motivic multiplicativity defect conjecture.** Any CK decomposition of $X$ is $m$-fold $mn$-multiplicative for every integer $m\geq 2$. In particular, 
$$
\mathfrak{d}_m(X)\leq mn.
$$
 This predicts a sharp linear bound on the obstruction to compatibility between multiple intersection products and CK decompositions; the paper presents it as a first step toward determining these defects, and no resolution is supplied.
technical_disposition: Every CK decomposition and every m>=2 require a Chow-correspondence defect bound, not a cohomological degree bound. Dimension vanishing alone does not clear homologically trivial components. Definitions/primary body unread; no finite certificate route.
title: The motivic multiple multiplicativity defect bound

source_name_as_recorded: Rafał Kalinowski, Monika Pilśniak, Elżbieta Sidorowicz and Elżbieta Turowska, “Quasi-majority neighbor sum distinguishing edge-colorings”, arXiv:2511.01835 (2025).
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with minimum degree $\delta(G)\geq 2$, and let $\chi_{\sum}^{M}(G)$ denote its majority neighbor sum distinguishing index. **Majority neighbor sum distinguishing conjecture.** Every graph $G$ with $\delta(G)\geq 2$ satisfies

$$
\chi_{\sum}^{M}(G)\leq 5.
$$

This conjecture is posed after bounds for majority neighbor sum distinguishing colorings, including a bound of 15 for graphs of minimum degree at least 4 and 12 for even-order graphs whose vertices all have even degree; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
technical_disposition: Universal five-label majority neighbor-sum bound at minimum degree2 simultaneously imposes local majority and unequal neighboring sums. Existing 12/15 bounds do not specialize to5; small graph feasibility would not yield universal construction. Definition body unread.
title: Majority neighbor sum distinguishing conjecture

source_name_as_recorded: Yangyang Cheng, Zhenyu Li, Wanting Sun and Guanghui Wang, “A step toward Chen-Lih-Wu conjecture”, arXiv:2511.03957 (2025).
statement:
Let an **equitable $k$-coloring** be a proper $k$-coloring whose color classes have sizes differing by at most one, and let $d(x)$ denote the degree of a vertex $x$. **Kierstead-Kostochka-Mydlarz-Szemerédi conjecture.** If $G$ is a graph with $d(x)+d(y)<2k$ for all $xy∈E(G)$, then there exists a polynomial-time algorithm to determine an equitable $k$-coloring of $G$.

This is the algorithmic counterpart of the Ore-type equitable-coloring conjectures. The source says it holds when $k$ is at least a fixed positive proportion of the order of $G$, while smaller values are not covered by the paper.
technical_disposition: Polynomial-time algorithm required uniformly in graph and k under every edge degree-sum constraint. Existence or a fixed-density k regime is insufficient. No algorithm with termination and polynomial complexity proof; no instance count as outcome.
title: Kierstead-Kostochka-Mydlarz-Szemerédi algorithmic Ore-type conjecture

source_name_as_recorded: Ronen Wdowinski, “Hall's theorem for reconfigurations and higher dimensional topological connectedness”, arXiv:2511.04863 (2025).
statement:
Let $H$ be an $r$-partite $r$-graph, let $A$ be one of its $r$ partition classes, and let $\mathbf{RG}_{\mathrm{Mat}}(H,A;k)$ denote the matching reconfiguration graph on matchings of size $k$. Let $\tau(H)$ be the minimum vertex-cover size. **Reconfiguration conjecture.** For $r\geq 2$, if

$$
k<\frac{\tau(H)}{r-1},
$$

then

$$
\mathbf{RG}_{\mathrm{Mat}}(H,A;k)
$$

is connected. This extends the proved $r=3$ reconfiguration result in the spirit of the Henderson–Ryser conjecture. The claim is stated as a conjecture for all uniformities $r\geq 2$; no resolution is supplied in the source.
technical_disposition: For all r>=2, matching size k below tau/(r-1) must imply connected matching reconfiguration graph. Need exact adjacency definition and full uniformity mechanism beyond r=3. No route from cover inequality to an admissible exchange sequence established.
title: Reconfiguration conjecture for multipartite hypergraphs

source_name_as_recorded: Hojin Chu, Shinya Fujita, Boram Park and Homoon Ryu, “Connectivity keeping trees in triangle-free graphs”, arXiv:2511.06622 (2025).
statement:
Throughout, graphs are finite, simple, and undirected; $\k$ and $\m$ are positive integers, the order of a graph is its number of vertices, and $\kappa(G)$ denotes its connectivity. A graph is $\k$-connected when $\kappa(G)\geq k$. A tree has order $\m$ when it has $\m$ vertices.

**Mader's conjecture.** For any tree $\T$ of order $\m$, every $\k$-connected graph $\G$ with minimum degree

$$
\delta(G)\geq \left\lfloor\frac{3k}{2}\right\rfloor+m-1
$$

contains a subtree $\T'\cong T$ such that

$$
\kappa(G-V(T'))\geq k.
$$

Mader proved the corresponding assertion for a path, and later obtained a weaker quadratic minimum-degree bound for arbitrary trees. The conjecture is known for $\k\leq 3$ and remains open for $\k\geq 4$; a linear minimum-degree sufficient condition is known.
technical_disposition: Every tree order m and every connectivity k require preservation after deleting its embedding at the sharp linear degree threshold. Greedy embedding alone cannot protect residual k-connectivity. Known paths/k<=3 are parameter cases; no full route.
title: Mader's connectivity-keeping tree conjecture

source_name_as_recorded: Qiuli Li, Fuliang Lu and Heping Zhang, “On minimal k-factor-critical planar graphs”, arXiv:2511.08137 (2025).
statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-factor-critical graph, meaning that deleting any $k$ vertices leaves a graph with a perfect matching. Call $G$ **minimal** if deleting any edge produces a graph that is not $k$-factor-critical. Write $(G)$ for the minimum vertex degree of $G$.

**Favaron–Shi's conjecture.** If $G$ is a minimal $k$-factor-critical graph, then

$$
\delta(G)=k+1.
$$

The conjecture was posed by Favaron and Shi and concerns the sharpness of the general lower bound on the minimum degree of minimal $k$-factor-critical graphs. It is known for several values of $k$, including $k=1$, $k\in\{n-6,n-4,n-2\}$, and $k\in\{2,n-10,n-8\}$, as well as for claw-free graphs; the source proves it for planar graphs.
technical_disposition: Minimal k-factor-critical graphs must attain minimum degree k+1 over all admissible orders and k. Planar/claw-free results do not cover arbitrary graphs. k=0 or empty boundary conventions are wording checks, not eligible outcomes; no structural minimality argument.
title: Favaron–Shi minimum-degree conjecture for minimal factor-critical graphs

source_name_as_recorded: Erica Flapan and Hugh Howards, “Minimal crossing diagrams of spatial graphs”, arXiv:2511.09712 (2025).
statement:
Let $L$ be a link. A diagram of $L$ is **reduced alternating** if it is alternating and has no nugatory crossings. The crossing number of $L$ is the minimum number of crossings among all diagrams of $L$.

**Tait's conjecture.** A reduced alternating diagram of $L$ has minimal crossing number, and if $L$ is prime then no non-alternating diagram has minimal crossing number.

This conjecture initiated the study of minimal crossing diagrams of links and was proved independently by Thistlethwaite, Kauffman, and Murasugi in 1987.
technical_disposition: Statement reports 1987 Tait resolution, including prime-link nonalternating minimality clause. No knot invariant proof body read here. Known-result/formalization work earns no new outcome.
title: Tait's conjecture on minimal crossing diagrams of links

source_name_as_recorded: Olaf Parczyk, Silas Rathke and Tibor Szabó, “The maximum diameter of 2-dimensional simplicial complexes”, arXiv:2511.10144 (2025).
statement: Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, let $C_n$ be a Hamilton cycle on these vertices, and let $C_n^2$ denote its square, obtained by joining pairs at distance at most two on the cycle. A **square-of-Hamilton-cycle decomposition conjecture.** For any $n \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, $n \not= 9$, there is a decomposition of $E(K_n)$ into copies of $C_n^2$. This strengthens the expected divisibility condition for packing squares of Hamilton cycles and is intended to guide explicit constructions; the cases $n=21,25,33,45,49,57,65,69$ are known, while $n=73$ is described as the smallest unresolved case.
technical_disposition: All admissible n congruent1 mod4 except9 require exact edge decompositions into Hamilton-cycle squares. Finite constructions and small n degeneracies cannot deliver uniform arithmetic construction. No all-order starter/difference mechanism available.
title: The exceptional-order conjecture for decomposing complete graphs into squares of Hamilton cycles

source_name_as_recorded: Olaf Parczyk, Silas Rathke and Tibor Szabó, “The maximum diameter of 2-dimensional simplicial complexes”, arXiv:2511.10144 (2025).
statement:
Let $H_s(n,d)$ denote the maximum diameter of a $d$-dimensional simplicial complex on $n$ vertices. The **simplicial-complex diameter conjecture.** For every $d\geq 3$, there is a threshold $n_0(d)$ such that, for all $n\geq n_0(d)$,

$$
H_s(n,d) = \left\lfloor \frac 1d \cdot \binom{n}{d} - \frac{d+1}{d} \right\rfloor.
$$

This asserts that the trivial upper bound is asymptotically tight in every dimension $d\geq 3$ and would determine the maximum diameter for all sufficiently large numbers of vertices. The source says that the detailed proof of the lower-bound strategy appears in a separate manuscript, while the matching upper-bound conjecture remains open.
technical_disposition: Each dimension d>=3 and every sufficiently large n require exact floor formula. A finite counterexample cannot defeat a dimension-dependent eventual threshold. Long induced-path constructions and convention on dimension need primary verification; no full route.
title: Polynomial Hirsch conjecture for simplicial-complex diameter

source_name_as_recorded: Marthinus Michael Dreeckmeier, “On the Fundamental Arithmetical Structure and Distribution of Lucky Numbers”, arXiv:2511.11657 (2025).
statement: Under the restricted factorization described in the source, assign a **fractional order** $\operatorname{ord}(p)$ or $\operatorname{ord}(l)$ recursively to primes $p$ and lucky numbers $l$: lucky primes have order $1$, products of powers of lucky primes have prime order $1/2$, and products of primes have lucky order $1/2$; in general, the order is determined by the smallest fractional order of the relevant factors as specified by the recursive definition. **Fractional-order infinitude conjecture.** For every fixed positive integer $n$, there are infinitely many prime numbers or lucky numbers of order $1/n$. This generalizes the conjecture that there are infinitely many lucky primes, but the source gives no resolution.
technical_disposition: Every fixed positive n requires infinitely many recursively defined fractional-order primes or lucky numbers. n=1 already reaches lucky-prime infinitude; a finite sieve is irrelevant. Restricted factorization definitions not recovered; no infinitude mechanism.
title: Infinitude of prime and lucky numbers of every fractional order

source_name_as_recorded: Yunling Chen, John Erik Fornæss and Song-Yan Xie, “Generating all Ahlfors currents by a single entire curve”, arXiv:2511.12473 (2025).
statement: Let $X$ be a projective manifold that is **rationally connected**, meaning that any two points of $X$ can be joined by a rational curve. Let Oka-1 denote the property that, for every open Riemann surface, compact Runge set, discrete interpolation sequence, and continuous map holomorphic near the relevant interpolation data, one can find a homotopic holomorphic map with the prescribed approximation and jet interpolation. **The Oka-1 conjecture.** Every rationally connected projective manifold is Oka-1. This is posed among open problems about weak Oka-1 manifolds; the source provides no resolution of the conjecture.
technical_disposition: Every rationally connected projective manifold with arbitrary open-Riemann-surface approximation and jet interpolation data is required. Rational curves through point pairs do not supply all Oka-1 approximation data. Large geometric dependency chain; no bounded constructive proof route.
title: The Oka-1 conjecture for rationally connected projective manifolds

source_name_as_recorded: Alexander Clow, Sean Kim and Ladislav Stacho, “A Note on Large Degenerate Induced Subgraphs in Sparse Graphs”, arXiv:2511.13693 (2025).
statement:
Let $\alpha_d(k)$ denote the infimum, over $k$-degenerate graphs, of the ratio of the order of a largest induced $d$-degenerate subgraph to the number of vertices. **Induced-degenerate-subgraph ratio conjecture for $k\geq 3$.** For all integers $k\geq 3$ and $d$ with $k>d$,

$$
\alpha_d(k)=\frac{d+1}{k+1}.
$$

This assertion is motivated by computational experiments and would determine the exact ratios for the indicated parameters. The source presents it as open.
technical_disposition: v1/v2 Conjecture4.2 read: all k>=3 and k>d. Clique gives upper ratio; partitioning a degeneracy ordering into classes of capacity d+1 only gives the sharp ratio when divisibility cooperates. No all-parameter lower bound or counterexample; no parameter-only proposal.
title: Exact induced-degenerate-subgraph ratio conjecture for k-degenerate graphs

source_name_as_recorded: Alexander Clow, Sean Kim and Ladislav Stacho, “A Note on Large Degenerate Induced Subgraphs in Sparse Graphs”, arXiv:2511.13693 (2025).
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges, and let $\alpha_1(G)$ denote the order of a largest induced $1$-degenerate subgraph of $G$, equivalently a largest induced forest. **Induced forest girth conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 3$, if $G$ has girth at least $k$, then

$$
\alpha_1(G)\geq n-\frac{m}{k}.
$$

The source notes that the bound would be best possible, as witnessed by a disjoint union of cycles of length $k$, and that the case of girth $3$ is trivial. The general assertion is presented as open.
technical_disposition: Actual v1 and v2 Conjecture4.5 have the unrestricted graph/girth quantifiers. Executed 24-vertex cubic girth7 certificate: 36 edges, removing s vertices leaves at least36-3s edges, so any nonempty induced forest requires36-3s<=23-s and s>=7. Thus alpha1<=17<132/7=24-36/7. Elementary cycle-rank/degree counting on a standard cubic graph; treated as uncredited classical adaptation, not discovery-cleared. No exact maximum, minimality or registry clearance claimed.
title: Induced forest bound for graphs of prescribed girth

source_name_as_recorded: Alexander Clow, Hitesh Kumar and Shivaramakrishna Pragada, “Improved Bounds for the Ultimate Independence Ratio of Odd Wheels”, arXiv:2511.18747 (2025).
statement:
Let $W_t$ be the join of the cycle $C_t$ with $K_1$, and let $d4b0(G)$ denote the ultimate independence ratio of a graph $G$. For odd wheels, $d4b0(W_{2t+1})$ is bounded below by $1/4$ because $d4b0(G)\geq 1/\chi(G)$ and $\chi(W_{2t+1})=4$. **Hahn–Hell–Poljak's conjecture.** For all integers $t\geq 1$, 
$$
\mathscr{I}(W_{2t+1})=\frac{1}{4}.
$$
 Determining the ultimate independence ratio of odd wheels is a central open problem in this setting; the $5$-wheel is identified as the smallest graph whose ratio is unknown.
technical_disposition: All odd wheels including t=1 require ultimate Cartesian-power independence ratio1/4. Finite powers only bound a limiting parameter and chromatic lower bound supplies one direction. No tensor-power upper certificate or full uniform argument.
title: Hahn–Hell–Poljak conjecture for odd wheels

source_name_as_recorded: Alexander Clow, Hitesh Kumar and Shivaramakrishna Pragada, “Improved Bounds for the Ultimate Independence Ratio of Odd Wheels”, arXiv:2511.18747 (2025).
statement:
Let $W_t$ be the join of the cycle $C_t$ with $K_1$, let $\alpha(G)$ be the independence number of $G$, and let $G\Box H$ denote the Cartesian product of graphs. For $t\geq 2$, consider the square $W_{2t+1}^{\Box 2}$ and its product with $K_3$. **Odd-wheel square subgraph conjecture.** For all $t\geq 2$, 
$$
(2t+2)\alpha(W_{2t+1})-\alpha(W_{2t+1}^{\Box 2}\Box K_3)=t-1.
$$
 Hence, the largest $3$-colourable subgraph of $W_{2t+1}^{\Box 2}$ has order $4t^2+5t+3$. This is motivated by computational observations and is presented as a future-work conjecture; no resolution is supplied.
technical_disposition: Displayed equation and following claimed value are inconsistent as written: alpha(W_(2t+1))=t makes displayed RHS solve to2t^2+t+1, not4t^2+5t+3. Product-vs-square/notation recovery from primary required. Wording correction is uncredited; no literal formula counterexample promoted.
title: Conjecture on the largest 3-colourable subgraph of odd-wheel squares

source_name_as_recorded: Tomasz Skalski and Tomasz Stroiński, “Level sets and maximum likelihood estimation for the Ising model”, arXiv:2511.20925 (2025).
statement:
Let $u(k,q)$ denote the size of the smallest set of uniqueness for the positive function class $\left(\mathcal{B}^{k}_{q}\right)_+$. In particular, consider the case $q=2$. **Minimum-size uniqueness conjecture.**

$$
u(k,2)=k+1,
$$

i.e., for every $k$ there are no sets of uniqueness having at most $k$ elements.
This conjecture concerns the exact minimum cardinality of a set of uniqueness in the $q=2$ case; the preceding results establish corresponding bounds, while the equality asserted here remains unresolved in the supplied text.
technical_disposition: All k require no uniqueness set of size<=k in a positive function class. Dimension heuristics do not prove existence of a positive function vanishing on arbitrary constraints; need exact class and positivity definitions. No primary definitions/body clearance.
title: Conjecture on the minimum size of uniqueness sets for the Ising model

source_name_as_recorded: Jianru Duan, “Universal L^2-torsion and sutured decomposition for 3-manifolds”, arXiv:2512.01305 (2025).
statement:
Let $F_1$ and $F_2$ be finitely generated free groups, let $\varphi\colon F_1\to F_2$ be a homomorphism, and let $\tau^{(2)}_u(\varphi)$ denote its universal $L^2$-torsion. **Universal $L^2$-torsion conjecture.** The homomorphism $\varphi$ is an isomorphism if and only if

$$
\tau^{(2)}_u(\varphi)=1.
$$

The conjecture seeks to determine how much group-theoretic information universal $L^2$-torsion detects. The source notes that Jaikin-Zapirain proved an $L^2$-homology characterization in the equal-rank injective case via compressed subgroups, while the stated equivalence for arbitrary homomorphisms between finitely generated free groups remains unresolved.
technical_disposition: Equivalence for arbitrary homomorphisms between finite-rank free groups requires torsion to be defined in the claimed scope, then detect surjectivity as well as injectivity. Equal-rank injective L2-homology result does not give arbitrary-map statement. Domain correction not credit; no route.
title: The universal $L^2$-torsion characterization of free-group isomorphisms

source_name_as_recorded: Bin Chen, Xinmin Hou and Xinyu Zhou, “Paths with two blocks in oriented graphs of large minimum semi-degree”, arXiv:2512.04423 (2025).
statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented graph, let $k$ be a positive integer, and write $\delta^{0}(D)$ for the minimum semi-degree. An **oriented path of length $k$** is a path on $k+1$ vertices with an arbitrary orientation of its edges.

**Stein's conjecture.** If

$$
\delta^{0}(D)>k/2,
$$

then $D$ contains every oriented path of length $k$.

This is the explicitly labelled conjecture introduced after earlier results on long directed paths and cycles. The supplied text gives no resolution status for it.
technical_disposition: Every arbitrary orientation of a k-edge path under minimum semidegree>k/2. Directed/two-block paths are special cases; greedy path growth does not handle alternating obstructions uniformly. No all-orientation embedding mechanism.
title: Stein's minimum semi-degree conjecture for oriented paths

source_name_as_recorded: Mikołaj Frączyk, “Infinitesimal containment and sparse factors of iid”, arXiv:2512.09301 (2025).
statement:
Let $G$ be a compact group with Haar probability measure $\mu$, let $\rho\colon\Gamma\to G$ be a homomorphism, and let $\Gamma$ act on $(G,\mu)$ by left translation through $\rho$. **Non-amenable image criterion.** If $\rho(\Lambda)$ is open in $G$ for every non-amenable subgroup $\Lambda$ of $\Gamma$, then 
$$
(G,\mu)\xhookrightarrow{\operatorname{inf}}\Gamma.
$$
 This is stated as a special case of the preceding compact-action conjecture and is presented as an open question supported only by the authors' inability to find counterexamples.
technical_disposition: For every compact action satisfying openness of each nonamenable subgroup image, require infinitesimal containment. Open-image information does not directly construct sparse factors/finite-model approximations. Amenable special case not a full proof; primary definitions unread.
title: Non-amenable image criterion for infinitesimal containment of compact actions

source_name_as_recorded: Jianjun Jin, “Complex exponential integral means spectra of univalent functions and the Brennan conjecture”, arXiv:2512.09330 (2026).
statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be the class of normalized univalent functions, let $\overline{\mathbf{S}}$ be the indicated closed Schwarzian space, let $S_f$ be the Schwarzian derivative of $f\in\mathcal{S}$, and let $\Lambda_\alpha$ be the functional in the source. **Lambda-maximizer Schwarzian norm conjecture.** For every $\alpha>0$, if $\Lambda_\alpha$ attains at least one maximum at $S_f\in\overline{\mathbf{S}}$ for some $f\in\mathcal{S}$, then

$$
\|S_f\|_{E_2}=6.
$$

The preceding text asks separately whether maxima exist; this conjecture concerns the norm of any such maximizer under the stated attainment hypothesis.
technical_disposition: Conditional on actual attainment, every Lambda-alpha maximizer must have Schwarzian norm6. Nonexistence or one extremal Koebe-type map would not prove universal conditional. Functional and E2 topology definitions missing from literal row; primary HOLD.
title: Schwarzian norm conjecture for maximizers of the functional Lambda

source_name_as_recorded: Gábor Damásdi, Balázs Keszegh, János Pach, Dömötör Pálvölgyi and Géza Tóth, “Coloring Geometric Hypergraphs: A Survey”, arXiv:2512.09509 (2025).
statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a hereditary family of hypergraphs. For $k\ge1$, let $m_k(\mathcal F)$ be the smallest integer $m$ such that every $m$-heavy hypergraph in $\mathcal F$ has a polychromatic $k$-coloring, with $m_k(\mathcal F)=\infty$ if no such integer exists. **Hereditary-family polychromatic coloring conjecture.** If

$$
m_2(\mathcal F)<\infty,
$$

then

$$
m_k(\mathcal F)<\infty
$$

for every $k\ge2$. The conjecture is known when $m_2(\mathcal F)=2$, in which case Berge proved $m_k(\mathcal F)=k$ for every $k$; it is open in general, and the hereditary hypothesis is necessary.
technical_disposition: Every hereditary hypergraph family with finite2-color threshold must have each finite k-color threshold. Repeated2-color splitting fails without control that each color class remains heavy; no hereditary restriction lemma supplying that control. Known threshold2 case insufficient.
title: The hereditary-family polychromatic coloring conjecture

source_name_as_recorded: Preston Kelley, “Areal Weil Heights”, arXiv:2512.16007 (2025).
statement:
Let $K$ be a number field, let $\mu$ be an adelic measure defined over $K$, let $h_\mu$ be its associated height on $\mathbb{P}^1(\overline{K})$, and let $\mathcal{L}(\mu)$ denote the energy infimum associated with $\mu$. **Lehmer-type conjecture above the energy minimum.** There exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that

$$
[K(\alpha):K]\bigl(h_\mu(\alpha)-\mathcal{L}(\mu)\bigr)\geq\varepsilon
$$

for every $\alpha\in\mathbb{P}^1(\overline{K})$ such that $h_\mu(\alpha)>\mathcal{L}(\mu)$.

This formulation is designed to remain meaningful when $\mathcal{L}(\mu)>0$. The supplied text subsequently discusses evidence that it fails for particular measures, but does not provide a resolution of the general assertion.
technical_disposition: Every adelic measure over each number field needs one positive epsilon across all algebraic points strictly above the energy minimum. Standard height-gap/Lehmer tools do not transfer to arbitrary adelic energies. Literal row already reports failure evidence; actual measure/counterexample body unread. No numerical-height proposal.
title: Lehmer-type conjecture for adelic heights above the energy minimum

source_name_as_recorded: Andreas Bluhm, Eric Evert, Igor Klep, Victor Magron and Ion Nechita, “Inclusion constants for free spectrahedra with applications to quantum incompatibility”, arXiv:2512.17706 (2025).
statement:
Let $s_{\mathbb C}(2,4)$ denote the minimum compatibility degree of four dichotomic measurements on a complex qubit. **Four-dichotomic-qubit compatibility-degree conjecture.**

$$
s_{\mathbb C}(2,4)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}.
$$

The value is attained by the displayed computational-basis and equiangular-line measurements, and numerical optimization provides evidence for optimality; a proof remains open.
technical_disposition: Global minimization over all four dichotomic qubit measurements. Attaining2/sqrt13 supplies one inequality only; need universal incompatibility bound and exact unbiased/biased reduction. No global algebraic dual certificate; numerical optimization not executed.
title: Four-dichotomic-qubit compatibility-degree conjecture

source_name_as_recorded: Peter Bradshaw, Abhishek Dhawan, Nhi Dinh, Shlok Mulye and Rohan Rathi, “Choosability of multipartite hypergraphs”, arXiv:2512.21222 (2025).
statement:
Let $k\geqslant 2$. A **$k$-partite $k$-graph** is a $k$-uniform hypergraph whose vertex set has a partition into $k$ parts such that every edge contains exactly one vertex from each part. Let $H$ be such a hypergraph with maximum degree at most $\Delta$, and let $\mathsf{ch}(H)$ denote its choice number.

**Dhawan's conjecture.** For every $k\geqslant 2$, there is a constant $c=c(k)>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $\Delta$,

$$
\mathsf{ch}(H)\leqslant c\log \Delta.
$$

This is a stronger uniform statement extending the bipartite-graph conjecture to all uniformities. A recent bound of order $(\Delta/\log\Delta)^{1/(k-1)}$ is known, but the conjectured logarithmic bound remains unresolved.
technical_disposition: Each fixed k>=2 needs c(k) logDelta lists for every sufficiently largeDelta multipartite hypergraph. Contains the bipartite graph case k2, so special higher-uniformity bounds do not settle it. No entropy/list-coloring mechanism at logarithmic scale.
title: Dhawan's multipartite hypergraph choosability conjecture

source_name_as_recorded: Bruce E. Sagan and Chenchen Zhao, “Properties of plactic monoid centralizers”, arXiv:2512.21401 (2025).
statement: A word $u$ has maximum letter $m$ and is **$m$-packed** if it contains at least one copy of every integer in $[m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}$. A word $u$ is **$m$-stable** when its centralizers satisfy $C(u^k)=C(u^{k+1})$ for the relevant stability range $m\le k$. **Stability conjecture.** If $u$ is $m$-packed, then $u$ is $m$-stable. This is supported by computations for $m=3,4$ and words of length at most $8$; the cases $m=1$ and $m=2$ were already established, but the general assertion remains open.
technical_disposition: All m-packed words of arbitrary multiplicity and all powers k>=m require equality of plactic centralizers. Bounded length or m3/4 computations cannot prove full stabilization; no tableau structural classification supplied. No word sweep executed.
title: Stability conjecture for packed words in the plactic monoid

source_name_as_recorded: Yan X Zhang, “Tiling Triangles with 2π/3 Angles”, arXiv:2512.22696 (2026).
statement:
Let $(a,b,c)$ be the side lengths of the triangular tile, and say that a positive real number $X$ is **equiconstructible** by $(a,b,c)$ when an equilateral triangle with side length $X$ can be tiled by copies of that triangle. **Divisibility conjecture.** All equiconstructible $X$ are divisible by $ab$; in particular, for the tile $(a,b,c)=(5,16,19)$, every equiconstructible $X$ is divisible by $16$.

The preceding lemma proves the divisibility statement when $a$ and $b$ are square-free, while the case $(5,16,19)$ is presented as the smallest interesting case beyond that result. The conjecture is intended to constrain the possible side lengths of equilateral tilings.
technical_disposition: Universal divisibility over equiconstructible real side lengths needs normalized integer tile hypotheses from primary. Rescaling arbitrary tile lengths destroys naive integer divisibility; such a domain correction earns no credit. Square-free lemma does not settle5,16,19; no coloring invariant.
title: The divisibility conjecture for equiconstructible equilateral triangles

source_name_as_recorded: Quanyu Tang and Hao Zhang, “Average first-passage times for character sums”, arXiv:2512.24631 (2026).
statement:
Let $
obreak\footcomment$ be omitted. For an odd prime $p$, write

$$
S_\ell(p):=\sum_{n\leq \ell}\left(\frac{n}{p}\right),
$$

where $\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ is the Legendre symbol modulo $p$. For $\varepsilon>0$, let $F_\varepsilon(p)$ be the smallest integer such that

$$
S_\ell(p)<\varepsilon\ell\qquad\text{for every }\ell\geq F_\varepsilon(p).
$$

**Erdős's eventual-time conjecture.** There exists a constant $C_\varepsilon>0$ such that

$$
\sum_{p\leq x}F_\varepsilon(p)\sim C_\varepsilon\,\frac{x}{\log x}.
$$

Erdős posed this as a question about the eventual time at which a quadratic character sum remains below a linear barrier. The conjecture was proved by Elliott.
technical_disposition: Literal statement explicitly credits Elliott with the eventual-time average asymptotic. Strict barrier definition and epsilon domain require source precision but do not create a new outcome. Actual Elliott body not read here.
title: Erdős's eventual-time conjecture for quadratic character sums

source_name_as_recorded: Ádám Sagmeister and Konrad J. Swanepoel, “Penny graphs in the hyperbolic plane”, arXiv:2512.24832 (2025).
statement:
Let $e_{d(7)}(n)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a penny graph with $n$ vertices and distance $d(7)$. **Exact edge-count conjecture.** For all $n
obreak\geq 1$, $e_{d(7)}(n)$ equals the upper bound from Theorem~. This conjecture asserts exactness of the proved upper bound for the order-$7$ triangular tiling; the supplied text gives no resolution beyond the stated upper bound and partial computational evidence.
technical_disposition: Although marked full, literal record omits the actual upper-bound formula and theorem number, and contains damaged n>=1 text. Cannot assess universal equality against an unspecified quantity. Primary formula recovery needed; metadata not technical clearance.
title: The exact edge-count conjecture for order-7 triangular tiling spirals

source_name_as_recorded: Lior Gishboliner, Zhihan Jin and Benny Sudakov, “Set mappings for general graphs”, arXiv:2601.00766 (2026).
statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $G$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph with $m$ edges and no isolated vertices. The parameter $w(G)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every map

$$
f:E(K_N^{(k)})\to E(K_N^{(k)})
$$

with $f(e)\cap e=\emptyset$ for every $e\in E(K_N^{(k)})$ admits a copy $G^*$ of $G$ in $K_N^{(k)}$ satisfying $f(e)\cap V(G^*)=\emptyset$ for every $e\in E(G^*)$. **Hypergraph linear-bound conjecture.** For every such $k$-graph $G$, one has

$$
w(G)=O(m).
$$

This would extend the paper's linear upper bound for graphs to uniform hypergraphs, but the authors note that their methods do not easily generalize to this setting.
technical_disposition: All fixed uniformities k require a linear-in-edge bound for set mappings avoiding their own edges. Randomly embedding G gives dependency terms involving high vertex degrees; graph proof does not automatically extend. No hypergraph deletion/embedding argument eliminating this obstruction.
title: Linear upper bound for set mappings of uniform hypergraphs

source_name_as_recorded: H. Tracy Hall, “The Delta Theorem: a dimension bound for faithful orthogonal graph representations”, arXiv:2601.01211 (2026).
statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, and let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree. The maximum nullity $\mathrm{M}(G)$ is the greatest nullity among matrices associated with $G$ in the maximum nullity problem. **Delta Conjecture.** For every simple graph $G$,

$$
\delta(G) \le \mathrm{M}(G).
$$

The conjecture arose in combinatorial matrix theory and is a lower bound on maximum nullity. It is known for all bipartite graphs and for complements of bipartite graphs, but the source does not report a complete resolution.
technical_disposition: Actual Hall2601.01211v1 section3.7 Corollary3.24 explicitly proves Delta; section5.6 main proof read. Chain delta<=greedegree<=Mpu<=nu<=M+<=M supplies exact subsumption. Main proof invokes Unique Monomial Lemma, not independently audited. Posted theorem defeats discovery eligibility regardless of conjecture metadata.
title: The Delta Conjecture for maximum nullity of graphs

source_name_as_recorded: H. Tracy Hall, “The Delta Theorem: a dimension bound for faithful orthogonal graph representations”, arXiv:2601.01211 (2026).
statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, and let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree. Write $\nu(G)$ for the greatest codimension of a faithful orthogonal representation whose Gram matrix has the Strong Arnold Property (SAP). **Strong Delta Conjecture.** For every simple graph $G$,

$$
\delta(G) \le \nu(G).
$$

This conjecture would strengthen Maehara's conjecture because $\nu(G)\leq \mathrm{M}_+(G)$. The source introduces it as a possible stronger conjecture and does not report a resolution.
technical_disposition: Same actual Hall body Corollary3.22 explicitly states Strong Delta holds. Section5.6 proof read with dependencies on3.9,5.3 and Unique Monomial Lemma; full dependency chain not audited. This is direct posted full-scope resolution, not an absence-of-search inference.
title: Strong Delta Conjecture for the SAP maximum nullity parameter

source_name_as_recorded: Avital Boruchovsky, Anina Gruica, Jonathan Niemann and Eitan Yaakobi, “Serving Every Symbol: All-Symbol PIR and Batch Codes”, arXiv:2601.04041 (2026).
statement:
Let $ASP(k,t,q)$ and $ASB(k,t,q)$ denote the minimum lengths of, respectively, all-symbol PIR and all-symbol batch codes with parameters $k,t,q$. For all $k,q$ and $t_1,t_2\geq 1$, **Subadditivity in $t$.**

$$
ASP(k,t_1+t_2,q)\leq ASP(k,t_1,q)+ASP(k,t_2,q),
$$

$$
ASB(k,t_1+t_2,q)\leq ASB(k,t_1,q)+ASB(k,t_2,q).
$$

The claim extends the known subadditivity results for functional PIR and batch codes; the paper notes that the corresponding general statement for all-symbol parameters remains open.
technical_disposition: All k,q,t1,t2 require both all-symbol PIR and batch subadditivity. Concatenating generator blocks serves message symbols but must recover each new parity symbol too; general all-symbol property is the missing bridge. No full construction; classical functional-code subadditivity is insufficient.
title: Subadditivity in t for all-symbol PIR and batch codes

source_name_as_recorded: Richard P. Anstee, Oakley Edens, Arvin Sahami, Jaehwan Seok and Attila Sali, “Exact Bounds for Forbidden Configurations and the Extremal Matrices”, arXiv:2601.04084 (2026).
statement:
Let $t$ be given, and let ${\mathrm{forb}}(m,F(0,2^{t-2}+1,1,0))$ denote the maximum number of columns in an $m$-rowed binary matrix avoiding the configuration $F(0,2^{t-2}+1,1,0)$. **Forbidden-configuration bound conjecture.**

$$
{\mathrm{forb}}(m,F(0,2^{t-2}+1,1,0))\leq \frac{2^{t}-1}{t}m+1,
$$

with equality when $m\equiv 0\pmod{t}$. The conjecture is motivated by constructions using the matrix $K_t$ and the matrices $B_i=K_t\backslash \mathbf{1}_t$, which attain the stated bound in the displayed cases; its validity for arbitrary $t$ is not established in the supplied text.
technical_disposition: All m and admissible t require sharp forbidden-configuration count and equality at every multiple of t. Kt block construction proves lower witness only. No induction controlling arbitrary simple matrices at exact slope; t boundary/domain recovery required.
title: The forbidden-configuration bound for binary matrices

source_name_as_recorded: Hyunwoo Lee, “Anticoncentration of random spanning trees in almost regular graphs”, arXiv:2601.07740 (2026).
statement:
Let $d_0,c>0$ be universal constants. For every integer $d\geq d_0$, let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree at least $d$, and let $\mathcal{T}$ be a uniformly random spanning tree of $G$. For every $n$-vertex tree $T$, **Minimum-degree anticoncentration conjecture.**

$$
\Pr\bigl[\mathcal{T}\simeq_{\mathrm{iso}}T\bigr]\leq n^{-c}.
$$

This proposes a polynomial anticoncentration bound under the minimum-degree assumption, which is substantially weaker than almost regularity. Complete bipartite graphs show that the paper's stronger exponential conclusions fail under this weaker hypothesis, but the authors note that such graphs still contain polynomially many pairwise non-isomorphic spanning trees.
technical_disposition: Universal d0,c and every n-vertex connected minimum-degree-d graph require polynomial anticoncentration for each tree isomorphism class. Labeled-tree counts do not control concentration on one unlabeled shape; high-degree hubs defeat almost-regular reductions. No switching argument uniform in irregularity.
title: Polynomial anticoncentration conjecture under a minimum-degree condition

source_name_as_recorded: Hitesh Kumar, Bojan Mohar, Shivaramakrishna Pragada and Hanmeng Zhan, “Convex combination of first and second eigenvalues of trees”, arXiv:2601.10036 (2026).
statement:
Let $G$ be any graph of order $n$, and let $\lambda_1(G)$ and $\lambda_2(G)$ denote its two largest adjacency eigenvalues. **Ebrahimi–Mohar–Nikiforov–Ahmady conjecture.** The spectral sum satisfies

$$
\lambda_1(G)+\lambda_2(G)\leq \frac{8n}{7}.
$$

The conjecture extends the extremal spectral-sum question from trees to arbitrary graphs. The supplied context states that analogous questions for graphs remain open and gives no resolution of this bound.
technical_disposition: For every graph the sum of its top two eigenvalues must be<=8n/7. Trace/norm estimates only yield weaker bounds; tree result is not arbitrary graph control. No rational quotient-matrix witness or global spectral inequality found; no numerical spectral sweep.
title: Ebrahimi–Mohar–Nikiforov–Ahmady conjecture on the spectral sum of graphs

source_name_as_recorded: Chenxing Li, Jiaao Li, Rong Luo and Bo Su, “High-Dimensional p-Normed Flows”, arXiv:2601.12036 (2026).
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let a **circular $(3+\epsilon)$-NZF** mean a circular nowhere-zero flow with parameter $3+\epsilon$. **Circular-flow threshold conjecture.** For $\epsilon\in[0,1]$, there exist two functions $f$ and $g$, with $f(\epsilon)\in[2,+\infty]$ strictly increasing and $g(\epsilon)\in[1,2]$ strictly decreasing, such that if $G$ admits a circular $(3+\epsilon)$-NZF, then

$$
\phi_{2,p}(G)=2 \quad \text{for all } p\ge f(\epsilon) \text{ and for all } 1\le p\le g(\epsilon).
$$

This conjecture seeks parameter ranges in which a circular-flow hypothesis forces the two-dimensional $p$-normed flow index to attain its minimum; no resolution is supplied.
technical_disposition: All epsilon in[0,1] need strict monotone thresholds at both low and high p with exact index2 for every qualifying graph. Endpoint/infinity wording alone would be uncredited; no flow-vector construction with simultaneous norm control. Primary definitions needed.
title: Circular-flow threshold conjecture for two-dimensional normed flows

source_name_as_recorded: Alexandr Buryak, Jianghao Xu and Di Yang, “Bihamiltonian tests for integrable systems associated to rank-1 F-CohFTs”, arXiv:2601.13203 (2026).
statement:
Consider an integrable hierarchy of scalar conservation laws

$$
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t_n}=\partial_x\omega_n,
$$

which is a perturbation of the Riemann--Hopf hierarchy, and transform it to the Arsie--Lorenzoni--Moro normal form

$$
\widetilde{\omega}_1=\frac{w^2}{2}+a(w)w_x+\sum_{k\geq2}\epsilon^k\sum_{\substack{\lambda\in\mathcal{P}_k\\m_1(\lambda)=0}}c_\lambda(w)w_\lambda.
$$

Assume $a(w)=0$ and $c_2(w)\neq0$. **Normal-form classification conjecture.** All coefficients $c_\lambda(w)$ with odd $|\lambda|$ vanish; the functions $c_2(w),c_4(w),\ldots$ uniquely determine every other $c_\lambda(w)$; and $c_2(w),c_4(w),\ldots$ are arbitrary free functional parameters. The source supplies no evidence of resolution for this stated claim.
technical_disposition: Every integrable scalar hierarchy in the specified normal form needs all odd coefficients zero, unique determination of mixed even coefficients and free choice of every even one. Finite perturbation-order checks cannot establish arbitrary-order integrability or existence. No generating-function recursion proving all obligations.
title: Normal-form classification conjecture for integrable RH conservation laws

source_name_as_recorded: Masaki Kashima, Riste Škrekovski and Rongxing Xu, “Degree-choosability of proper conflict-free list coloring of sparse graphs”, arXiv:2601.15611 (2026).
statement: For a graph $G$, write $d_G(v)$ for the degree of a vertex $v$. A $({\rm degree}+1)$-list assignment assigns each vertex $v$ a list $L(v)$ with $|L(v)|\geq d_G(v)+1$. A graph is **proper conflict-free $({\rm degree}+1)$-choosable** if it has a proper conflict-free $L$-coloring for every such list assignment. **Degree-plus-one conjecture.** Every connected graph of minimum degree at least $3$ is proper conflict-free $({\rm degree}+1)$-choosable. This seeks a one-color improvement over the general degree-plus bound for graphs without vertices of degree below three, and remains open according to the source.
technical_disposition: All connected min-degree3 graphs and arbitrary degree+1 lists need proper coloring with a unique-colored neighbor at every vertex. Greedy proper coloring consumes available slack and does not enforce neighbor uniqueness. Sparse graph results not full scope; no reducible-configuration closure.
title: Degree-plus-one conjecture for graphs of minimum degree three

source_name_as_recorded: Daniel Iľkovič and Jun Yan, “Distribution of independent sets in perfect r-ary trees”, arXiv:2601.16953 (2026).
statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, let $k\geq 1$, and let $\mathcal{I}_{T}^{k}(v)$ denote the family of independent sets of size $k$ in $T$ containing $v$. A **leaf-centred maximum-star conjecture.** There exists a leaf $\ell$ of $T$ such that

$$
|\mathcal{I}_{T}^{k}(v)|\leq|\mathcal{I}_{T}^{k}(\ell)|
$$

for every $v\in V(T)$. This conjecture was disproved by independent work of Baber and Borg, which produced counterexamples for every $k\geq 5$.
technical_disposition: Literal statement explicitly reports Baber/Borg counterexamples for every k>=5. The assertion is already refuted as a universal tree claim. Original counterexample bodies unread here; do not search a smaller witness for credit.
title: Hurlbert–Kamat leaf-centred maximum-star conjecture for trees

source_name_as_recorded: Daniel Neuen and Tim Seppelt, “Distinguishing Graphs by Counting Homomorphisms from Sparse Graphs”, arXiv:2601.18602 (2026).
statement: For a graph $G$, its **Hadwiger number** is the largest integer $t$ such that $G$ contains the complete graph $K_t$ as a minor. Two graphs are homomorphism indistinguishable over a graph class if they admit the same number of homomorphisms from every graph in that class. **Roberson's weak conjecture.** For every $k \geq 0$, there exist non-isomorphic graphs $G$ and $H$ that are homomorphism indistinguishable over all graphs of Hadwiger number $\leq k$. This is a concrete form of the question whether sparse graph classes can distinguish all non-isomorphic graphs. The paper proves the conjecture for vortex-free graph classes, while the general minor-excluded case remains unresolved.
technical_disposition: Each Hadwiger bound k needs nonisomorphic graphs indistinguishable by all bounded-Hadwiger test graphs. Constructing equal counts on a finite set of tests is insufficient. Vortex-free-class theorem does not cover arbitrary excluded-minor classes; no full construction.
title: Roberson's weak conjecture for bounded Hadwiger number

source_name_as_recorded: Beth Bjorkman, Sean English and Johnathan Koch, “Cost-Benefit Analysis for PMU Placement in Power Grids”, arXiv:2601.19775 (2026).
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\underline{f}(G)$ for the minimum fort size of $G$, let $\mathrm{MObs}(G;i)$ denote the marginal observance at step $i$, and let $\gamma_P(G)$ denote the power domination number. For a positive integer $k$, write $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$. **Minimum-fort-size conjecture.** If

$$
\underline{f}(G)\geq 4,
$$

then

$$
\mathrm{MObs}(G;i)\geq 4
$$

for all $i\in[\gamma_P(G)]$. This asks whether the relationship between minimum fort size and marginal observances established for smaller minimum fort sizes extends to minimum fort size at least four; its status is not resolved in the source.
technical_disposition: Actual Conjecture4.1, fort definition, maxObs marginal definition and Lemma3.6 proof read. Generalizing the three-vertex gain needs a new local structural lemma when every closed neighborhood meets residual fort in at most3 vertices. Published grid example defeats stronger gain>=fortsize but only gives gain6, so does not refute gain4. No small certificate or full lemma established; no graph sweep.
title: The minimum-fort-size conjecture for marginal observances

source_name_as_recorded: Zach Hunter, Cosmin Pohoata, Jacques Verstraete and Shengtong Zhang, “Large point-line matchings and small Nikodym sets”, arXiv:2601.19879 (2026).
statement:
Let $\mathrm{IM}(d,q)$ denote the maximum size of an induced matching in the point-line incidence graph of $\mathbb{F}_q^d$. **High-dimensional induced matching conjecture.** For every fixed $d\ge 3$, 

$$
\mathrm{IM}(d,q)=o(q^d)\qquad\text{as }q\to\infty.
$$

Beyond the planar case, essentially no nontrivial upper bounds are known for point-line induced matchings in $\mathbb{F}_q^d$ when $d\ge 3$; even a qualitative improvement over the trivial bound $\mathrm{IM}(d,q)\le q^d$ would be significant.
technical_disposition: For every fixed d>=3 need induced matching density tending to zero uniformly through finite fields. Fixed q or one coordinate slice gives no asymptotic upper bound in full dimension. No removal/finite-field incidence theorem bridge; no enumeration.
title: The high-dimensional point-line induced matching conjecture

source_name_as_recorded: Zach Hunter, Cosmin Pohoata, Jacques Verstraete and Shengtong Zhang, “Large point-line matchings and small Nikodym sets”, arXiv:2601.19879 (2026).
statement:
Let $\mathrm{IM}(2,q)$ denote the maximum size of an induced matching in the point-line incidence graph of $\mathbb{F}_q^2$. **Prime-field planar induced matching conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large primes $q$,

$$
\mathrm{IM}(2,q)\le q^{3/2-c}.
$$

For arbitrary prime powers, Vinh's finite-field Szemerédi–Trotter theorem gives $\mathrm{IM}(2,q)\le q^{3/2}+q$, and this exponent is sharp up to constants when $q$ is a square because of the Hermitian unital. The conjecture asks for a power-saving improvement over this bound over prime fields.
technical_disposition: Requires one absolute positive power saving over exponent3/2 for all large prime fields. Excluding square-field Hermitian examples is not an upper bound; qualitative o(q^1.5) alone insufficient. No sum-product/incidence mechanism with required uniform exponent.
title: The prime-field planar induced matching conjecture
